body.statement: Consider a sequence of finite populations of fixed-dimensional vectors assigned by complete randomization to a fixed number of groups whose limiting proportions are positive. If every scalar projection satisfies the finite-population maximum-influence condition and the correlation matrices converge, then the coordinatewise variance-standardized vector of group-contrast estimators converges in distribution to the centered Gaussian vector having the limiting correlation matrix.

source.verbatim_statement: and the correlation matrix of τ̂(A) has a limiting value V, then (15) holds.

attestation.note: Directly checked arXiv:1610.04821v4 primary PDF on 2026-09-14. Theorem 4 states the coordinate-standardized vector CLT under condition (14) and limiting correlation V; Corollary 2 reduces condition (14) to the maximum-distance/finite-population-variance condition under additive effects.
